## This tag leaks credentials. Do not use it.

The worst of the six, and not because the leak is the largest. Its one functional change
traded a cosmetic complaint for a security regression, and it shipped a test that pinned
the leak as correct behaviour. The suite was green the whole time.

**It stays resolvable on purpose.** Deleting a tag buys nothing against an attacker, since
clones, forks and cached commit views all survive it, and it breaks anyone already pinned
here. The disclosure record is the reason to trust the current release, so it is not being
quietly dropped.

**Be precise about whose credentials leaked.** The library failed to redact ITS USERS'
secrets: a credential a caller passed into `SecretRedactor.redact` could survive the
redactor and reach the model. No credential belonging to the author has ever been in this
repository, and every credential-shaped string under `Tests/` is synthetic.

## What is wrong with it

- **Every `NAME=value` secret shorter than 40 characters went out in plaintext.** A
  40-character floor was applied to the labelled form, and a labelled credential does not
  have to be long: `HF_TOKEN=`, `DB_PASS=` and most session identifiers sit well under it.
- **A test pinned that leak as correct.** It asserted `redact(s) == s` against a
  live-shaped bearer token, so the next person to fix the leak would have had to delete an
  assertion that looked deliberate. This is the reason
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) forbids
  pinning a known defect with an equality assertion, and requires `XCTExpectFailure`
  instead, so that fixing the bug turns the suite red and forces the fixer to delete the
  expectation deliberately.

Both were fixed in 0.4.0, which carries leaks of its own.

## What it fixed

Label swallowing, the NAT64 local-use prefix, and version signposting.

## What to use instead

**0.6.1**, or at minimum 0.5.0, which is the first tag with no known credential leak. Note
that the module is `GruxKit` up to and including 0.5.0 and `Grux` from 0.6.0 onward.

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux-guardrails.git", from: "0.7.0")
.product(name: "GruxGuardrails", package: "grux-guardrails")
```

## Full record

The complete narrative, including the wrong first attempts, is in
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). The README
section [Earlier tags leak credentials](https://github.com/dotcomjack/grux#earlier-tags-leak-credentials)
lists what each of the six leaking tags does.
